name: Large Behavior Models
summary: TRI ran roughly 1,800 real-robot rollouts plus thousands of simulated ones under blind, randomized A/B protocols with proper statistical treatment, testing whether large multitask diffusion pretraining beats single-task baselines. It does: pretrained models need several times less task-specific data and improve steadily with pretraining scale. The study also documents how easily sloppy evaluation manufactures illusory gains.
innovation: Blind, randomized, statistically powered real-robot evaluation methodology for manipulation.
Separated the true value of multitask pretraining from evaluation noise.
matters: A needed corrective in a field where most claims rest on a few dozen unblinded trials.
limits: Closed models; the contribution is methodological rather than a released artifact.
lineage: Diffusion-policy-based multitask models, evaluated with unusual statistical discipline.
